readThisFirst: THE LIST OF HERON PRODUCTS. Read as DATA and never executed - R-13, D-91, Golden Rule 19.
Adding a product is a line here plus a release asset. It is NEVER a rebuild of the installer
(R-3, D-93). If a product id appears in the installer's own code, that rule has been broken.
TWO KINDS OF ENTRY, AND NOTHING IN CODE TELLS THEM APART.
An entry that some other entry names in 'partOf' is a HEADING: it is a tab built by its pieces,
so it installs nothing itself and carries addin, assembly and addInId as null. Every other entry
installs itself and carries all three. The shape is derived from partOf alone, which is what
D-93 means by 'the same field drives the window's indentation and nothing is special-cased'.
ONE HEADING HAS TWO PIECES TODAY: 'heron'. That is S3 / D-89 and it is the only exception.
Heron Doc and Heron MEP are one tick each, whole tab.
THREE STATES, AND ONLY ONE OF THEM MAY BE OFFERED TO A USER.
SHIPPED   the files exist and a user may be offered this.
PROVING   the files exist and build, but they are a STAGE 2 SHAPE PROOF carrying one
dummy button. An installer MUST NOT offer one. They are deleted when Stage 2
closes and the real product replaces them, GUID and all.
PLANNED   the files do not exist yet. An installer MUST NOT offer one either.
The addInId is allocated here anyway, and on purpose: a GUID must be unique for ever, a
duplicate is a Revit load failure rather than a warning, and allocating them from one file is
what stops two sessions generating the same one by accident.
folder is where this product's files land, under Addins\<version>\. It is NOT derived from
the assembly name: heron-bridge's assembly is Heron.Revit.Addin.dll but its folder is Heron,
and that is the live layout on every machine Heron is installed on today. Deriving it would
silently move an existing install and orphan the one Revit is already loading.
requires is EMPTY everywhere, and since 2026-09-21 that is a DECISION rather than a silence.
Q-PE-2 is answered: the AI connector is optional everywhere and the tools work without it -
the owner's words were 'if they do not tick the AI connector, it will not be installed'. So
nothing requires anything, and the empty list now says so rather than deferring.
THE CONSEQUENCE IS NOT SMALL, and it belongs beside the list it follows from: a tool's button
cannot assume the bridge is there. Every button must work with the connector absent and may
offer the AI only as EXTRA when it is present - a button that errors without the bridge makes
the connector required in practice while this file says it is optional.
This block said 'Q-PE-2 and the owner has not ruled' until 2026-09-21, which was true when it
was written and is the opposite of true now (FRAGMENT-ISSUES row 5b-76).
Checked by tools/check-products.py. Run it after every edit to this file.
